_about: Titan overlay: replaces the Moon's milestone list (arrays replace). Ids are distinct from the Moon's and Mars's, because records are kept per campaign. Rules in rules/milestones.ts and rules/titanMilestones.ts (T5); zones come from the Titan terrain.json features. See game-design.md, How the Titan milestones work.
_interface: money and rp are placeholders set with Owner A, sized like Mars: a rover that only survives at the lander earns about 270 with the survival payout; an active camera run about 2.5 times that, a drill run about 3 times.

milestones.name: Touchdown
milestones.summary: The rover has landed in an interdune corridor of the Shangri-La dune field on Titan and deployed from the lander.
milestones.fact: On January 14, 2005, ESA's Huygens probe made the first landing on Titan. Its pictures show rounded pebbles of water ice on a dark plain.
milestones.source: ESA, Cassini-Huygens (esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/Cassini-Huygens); Tomasko et al. 2005, Nature 438:765

milestones.name: Odometer
milestones.fact: NASA's Dragonfly will not drive on Titan: it will fly from site to site, covering about 115 km in its planned mission.

milestones.name: Mapper
milestones.summary: The rover has surveyed {share}% of the map.
milestones.fact: Titan's haze hides its surface from visible-light cameras, so Cassini mapped it with radar, which sees through the haze, in details about 300 m across.
milestones.source: Radebaugh et al. 2008, Icarus 194:690 (Cassini RADAR dunes at about 300 m per pixel); NASA Science, Cassini (science.nasa.gov/mission/cassini/)

milestones.name: Dune crossing
milestones.summary: The rover has crossed a dune crest from one interdune corridor to the next.
milestones.fact: Titan's linear dunes are about 1 to 2 km wide and up to about 150 m high, and run west to east, often 10 to 100 km long, like the dunes of the Namib Desert on Earth.
milestones.source: Radebaugh et al. 2008, Icarus 194:690; Lorenz et al. 2021, Planet. Sci. J. 2:24

milestones.name: Night drive
milestones.summary: Distance driven during the long Titan night: {meters} m.
milestones.fact: A night on Titan lasts about eight Earth days. Dragonfly will spend it on the ground, recharging its battery from its nuclear power source.
milestones.source: NASA Science, Radioisotope Power Systems missions: Dragonfly (science.nasa.gov/radioisotope-power-systems-missions/); NASA NSSDC Saturnian satellite fact sheet

milestones.name: Dawn
milestones.summary: The rover is still running as the Sun rises again over the dunes.
milestones.fact: One Titan day lasts almost 16 Earth days. Titan always keeps the same face toward Saturn, so it turns once in each 16-day orbit.
milestones.source: NASA NSSDC, Saturnian satellite fact sheet (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/saturniansatfact.html); NASA Science, Dragonfly

milestones.name: Storm survivor
milestones.summary: The rover is still running after the methane rain has cleared.
milestones.fact: In late 2010 Cassini saw a huge cloud system near Titan's equator. Afterwards more than 500,000 km² of ground looked darker, most likely wet from methane rain.
milestones.source: Turtle et al. 2011, Science 331:1414; ESA, Turtle et al. 2011 summary (sci.esa.int/web/cassini-huygens/-/48586-turtle-e-p-et-al-2011)

milestones.name: Dune sea
milestones.summary: The rover has photographed the dune field from a dune crest.
milestones.fact: Titan's dunes form a belt around its equator. In a single radar image strip, Cassini measured more than 2,300 of them.
milestones.source: Radebaugh et al. 2008, Icarus 194:690 (2,315 dunes in the T3 swath)

milestones.name: Organic sands sample
milestones.summary: The rover has drilled a sample of the dune field's organic sands.
milestones.fact: Titan's dune sand is thought to be organic material, not rock like most sand on Earth. Cassini's infrared and radar data point to it, but nobody has sampled it yet.
milestones.source: Lorenz et al. 2021, Planet. Sci. J. 2:24 (conclusion); Radebaugh et al. 2008, Icarus 194:690

milestones.name: Crater ejecta
milestones.summary: The rover has drilled into the ejecta blocks of Selk crater.
milestones.fact: Selk is an impact crater about 80 km across. The impact may have melted ice into liquid water that mixed with organic material, which is why Dragonfly is going there.
milestones.source: NASA Science, Dragonfly (science.nasa.gov/mission/dragonfly/); Lorenz et al. 2021, Planet. Sci. J. 2:24; IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Selk

milestones.name: Clean run
milestones.summary: The mission has ended without any damage to the rover.
milestones.fact: Dragonfly flies instead of driving partly to avoid Titan's potentially rough and sandy ground: its rotors carry it over the dunes.
milestones.source: NASA Science, Dragonfly spacecraft and instruments (science.nasa.gov/mission/dragonfly/spacecraft-and-instruments/)
